name: ranjan-iykyknow-ai/ant-signal-lens
method: Supply-aware paired IPO paths; primary-source evidence gates, fixed-seed scenarios and sensitivity audit
thesis: A filing-grounded supply-risk view with a frozen information cutoff. The November 17 S-1/A3 retains a $70-$78 range for 825 million offered shares and discloses up to 315 million additional shares potentially eligible for first-day sale, subject to the filing resale, lock-up and other conditions; eligibility is not actual selling. Code samples 30,000 joint paths from six sourced prior technology IPOs and a disclosed soft/filed/above-range pricing mixture. Opening, intraday and day-five returns share the same sampled IPO. The potential supply ratio shrinks historical return patterns toward conservative priors; its coefficient and scenario weights are assumptions, not learned causal effects. Other issuer disclosures and NVIDIA results remain context-only. The audit preserves original-source independence, conservative publication bounds and first-observed timestamps. p10/p90 are model-scenario quantiles, not demonstrated 80% market coverage. No live X collection or automatic author-accuracy scoring is claimed.
key_risks: Six deliberately selected technology IPOs are a small, biased comparison set for a much larger offering.
The filing range can change and the deal can price above it; scenario weights are subjective assumptions.
Up to 315 million potentially eligible shares are subject to resale and other conditions; eligibility does not imply actual selling.
Market reactions and AI-sector developments after the frozen cutoff can change opening and day-five demand.
Supply shrinkage and return priors are untrained; the small diagnostic does not establish accuracy or 80% interval coverage.
